mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances when the federal funds rate increases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the potential economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances when the unemployment rate increases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in housing starts by more than 10% in a month signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which often leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as it indicates a broader economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 50% of the instances when housing starts drop by more than 10% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as it indicates robust economic activity.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances when industrial production increases by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 4.5% and the CPI is increasing by more than 0.3% in a month, it indicates a high inflation environment with tight monetary policy, which historically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.3% in 1 month
regime_hint: high inflation with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 50% of the instances when both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate decreases by more than 0.2%, it signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as it indicates robust economic activity.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances when both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures by more than 1% over three months signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as it indicates a healthy economic expansion.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances when real personal consumption expenditures increase by more than 1% over three months.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth is negative for two consecutive quarters, it signals a recessionary environment, which historically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate a broader economic slowdown.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 is negative for 2 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 50% of the instances when GDP growth is negative for two consecutive quarters.
